first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down 4-6% QoQ, creating a durable engagement problem that directly impacts long-term revenue quality. Memory_31 and memory_86 show that simplification and shortening onboarding durably improve completion and adoption without the retention risks flagged in memory_73 (promotional pricing) or the scaling limits of memory_57 (referral incentives work only for established customers). Memory_91 shows activation messaging also works, but onboarding completion is the upstream lever—fixing that barrier will compound activation gains. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is valuable but doesn't address the SMB activation decline. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm whether the field-reduction and messaging approaches remain reliable at current scale. A simplification experiment targets the root problem (completion/activation decay), avoids the retention risk of competitive pricing responses, and is orthogonal to referral incentives (can be layered later). This preserves optionality while directly addressing the immediate performance drop.

final.rationale: The archive confirms memory_91 (activation messaging) delivered +6% activation with +1% retention lift and no downside risk. Memory_31 (signup simplification) shows +9% activation but -1% retention decay on SMB, creating uncertainty about net qualified revenue impact in current conditions where we're already losing price-sensitive accounts to competitors. Activation messaging is the safer lever: it improves engagement without introducing retention friction, it worked across the full user base (not segment-limited like memory_31), and it directly addresses the 6% activation decline. Given that onboarding completion is only down 4% but activation is down 6%, the gap suggests users are reaching the product but not engaging meaningfully—exactly what activation messaging targets. This experiment avoids promotional pricing (memory_73 risk), doesn't rely on established customer base (memory_57 constraint), and preserves the option to layer signup simplification later if needed. The +1% retention gain also buffers against competitive pressure.
